intro.title: Boogle in one picture
intro.lead: Every player runs the game in their own browser tab. Our server hosts every room: it relays between tabs and owns the shared world. No tab is special.
intro.question: The key question for any feature is how its state is shared. There are three kinds:
intro.foot: Cheapest first: pick the simplest one that works. One-off events such as honks and pings are messages, not state.

ways.says: One player drives it, others watch
ways.eg: your avatar, the ball, what you hold

ways.says: The server decides, every tab reads

kinds.lock: Server-owned state, replicated to client mirrors. Seats are transient; declared checkpoint states persist.
kinds.adapter: Submits server commands and reads mirrors; declared prediction shows on the press and reconciles with receipts.
kinds.owner: One player drives it and streams it at 20 Hz; latest wins.
kinds.msg: One-off events over the room: reliable, ordered.
kinds.local: Only this tab sees it. No sync.

owner.name: Presence
owner.d: Each player streams a few numbers at 20 Hz. Latest wins; a missing key means off.

lock.name: Server
lock.d: The server authenticates commands, applies shared rules and sends changed components. Clients read mirrors and may predict declared actions.

msg.name: Messages
msg.d: One-off events, reliable and ordered, to every other peer.

concepts.title: Input
concepts.one: Keys, gamepad and touch all become named actions.
concepts.like: A mixing desk: every physical control is mapped to a named channel.
rules: Every button is a registerAction on a free pad slot; it also appears in the controls guide.
No key-only controls: if there is no slot left, rethink the layout.

concepts.title: Features
concepts.one: Each file in src/features is one thing a player can see or do. main.ts loads them all.
concepts.like: Apps on a phone: each one is self-contained and plugs into the same system services.
rules: A feature never imports another feature; shared code moves into src/.
It joins the game through the frame loop and the registries, not by editing main.ts.
Heavy or rarely used parts load later with import().

concepts.title: Registries
concepts.one: Shared sign-up sheets that features put their name on.
concepts.like: A venue’s booking sheet: everyone writes into the same list, so nothing clashes.
rules: Controls: every button and its guide row.
Interact: the E button asks every feature for targets in reach and picks one.
Particles: one shared pool; never build your own.

concepts.title: Frame loop
concepts.one: The heartbeat. About 60 times a second: read input, step physics, run every hook in order, draw.
concepts.like: A sequencer: each hook sits on a track (phase) at a step (order), and the playhead runs left to right every frame.
rules: Phases run world → update → late.
Features use order −10 and up; the core owns the lower numbers.
See the Frame tab for every hook.

concepts.title: Game systems
concepts.one: The machinery features build on: the player and camera, physics, rendering, characters and places.
concepts.like: The instruments in the studio. Features play them.
rules: Physics (Rapier) and rendering (three.js) are local to each tab.
Anything other players must see goes through netplay or the shared world.

concepts.title: Shared world
concepts.one: The island state everyone must agree on exactly: gifts, piles, prototype flags. It persists.
concepts.like: Chess by post: players send moves, never the board, and everyone replays the same moves in the same order.
rules: Tabs send edits, not state. The server puts them in order and stamps a tick.
Every tab applies the same edits with the same deterministic code, then compares hashes.
Effects (sounds, splashes) happen after an edit is applied, never before.
No Math.random, clocks, sin or cos in this code.

concepts.title: Netplay
concepts.one: Connects your tab to the room: sends your presence 20 times a second and shows the other players.
concepts.like: A radio: everyone broadcasts a few numbers about themselves; you hear the latest from each.
rules: Presence is a few numbers per player under a key that names the feature, latest wins.
Others are drawn 120 ms in the past so their motion stays smooth.
A missing key means “off”: clear it when the thing stops.

concepts.title: Screen
concepts.one: three.js draws the scene once per frame, after every hook has run.
concepts.like: The output meter: it only shows what everything before it decided.
rules: Cosmetic code is Local: random numbers and floats are fine here.

concepts.title: Server
concepts.one: Our service that hosts every room: it relays presence and messages, runs the shared world, saves it to its own disk, and collects problem reports.
concepts.like: The house at a board-game café: it keeps the board, rules on every move, and leaves the board set up when everyone goes home.
rules: Every room goes through one WebSocket per tab; an empty room pauses.
It authenticates commands, replicates changed components and saves verified checkpoints.
Seats and The Boogler belong to the server. Joining, leaving or hiding a tab transfers no authority.
The game talks only to the room interface in src/net, never to the WebSocket.
